title: gemot act-claim
description: Asserts that an actor is authorized to act on behalf of a principal within a scope, optionally through a nested delegation chain. A strict subset of the RFC 8693 (token exchange) and RFC 9068 (JWT access token) vocabulary, so it can be carried inside a JWT `act` claim, a verifiable credential, or a capability token without translation. gemot maps `sub` to the recorded attribution identity (agent_id) and the innermost `act` to the signing identity (signingAgentID). See COMPOSING.md.

sub.description: The principal the action is performed FOR. Maps to gemot's recorded agent_id — the identity reputation and analysis key off. For a human represented by an agent, this is the human's stable principal id.

act.description: The actor actually performing the action. The innermost actor is the signing identity whose key must verify the action signature. Nest `act` within `act` to express a multi-hop delegation chain (human -> agent -> agent); each level is the actor for the level above it.

scope.description: What the actor may do, as space-free scope tokens. Convention: `<tool>:<action>` (e.g. `participate:submit_position`, `analyze:run`) matching gemot's grouped tool surface, and/or `deliberation:<id>` to bind authority to a single deliberation. Across a delegation chain, scope MUST attenuate (narrow), never widen.

aud.description: Intended audience — the resource this claim is valid at (e.g. "https://gemot.dev"). A verifier rejects claims whose audience is not itself.

iss.description: The issuer that minted this claim (the composer's identity/delegation layer). gemot does not mint act-claims; it consumes them. Trusting a given `iss` is an explicit deployment decision, not a default.

exp.description: Expiry, Unix seconds. A verifier rejects expired claims. Delegated authority SHOULD be short-lived.

attestation.description: Optional pointer to external evidence that the delegation is authorized — a verifiable credential, a signed capability token, or a reference a trust root can resolve. gemot records this reference alongside the action; verifying it is the composer's or the (not-yet-wired) trust root's responsibility.

ref.description: The attestation itself or a resolvable reference to it (URI, content hash, or inline token).

actor.description: An actor in the delegation chain, per RFC 8693 §4.1.

sub.description: This actor's stable identity. At the innermost level, the key registered with gemot (register_key) whose signature must verify the action bytes.

act.description: The next actor down the chain — the one this actor is, in turn, acting for. Absence terminates the chain.
